virtual reality can be a useful therapeutic tool in the treatment of certain mental disorders and that the therapeutic use of virtual reality should be based on the patient's individual needs.

media objects can be used to mobilize the symbolic function of the psyche, but that the processing and integration of the activated states of mind and affective experiences fails in the context of media addiction.
the virtual reality of computer games can be understood as a psychic reality, which can be experienced by gamers as an inner reality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the virtual reality of computer games is linked to the psychic reality of the player.
the question of what happens in the psychic reality of a person who is addicted to media and what happens to the person when they leave the media.

the question of whether and how the analytic setting can help the child/adolescents who are addicted to the virtual world of the computer to develop their psychic reality and to become more capable of coping with the real world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
virtual reality is an extension of the psyche, and that the psyche is an extension of virtual reality.
media addiction is not a specific disease but a symptom of a disturbed psychic reality, which is not yet able to be symbolically represented.

media addiction can be seen as a symptom of an underlying psychic disorder and that the use of virtual reality can be understood as a form of self healing, but only if it is integrated into the psychic reality.

the analytic relationship is the place where the symbolic and the imaginary can be reactivated and re-experienced, and that the analytic relationship can also serve as a model for the development of a psychic reality.

the virtual reality of the computer game is an attempt to heal the psyche by the psyche, but that the analytic relationship offers the possibility to integrate the virtual experience in the real world of the patient's life.
virtual reality can only be experienced and integrated in the context of a reality, which is not virtual.

the use of virtual reality is not a substitute for psychoanalysis.
we need to develop a psychoanalytic understanding of the impact of virtual reality and other media on the human psyche.
